title: Check: cluster architecture
description: Five questions on the two node roles, the API server's position and the path of `kubectl apply`.

questions.prompt: What separates a control plane node from a worker node?

options.text: Control plane nodes have more memory
Control plane nodes make decisions; workers run your containers
Workers cannot run any Kubernetes components
A node can only ever be one or the other

questions.explanation: The split is by responsibility, not hardware. And a node can be both - in a single-node kind or minikube cluster it is.

questions.prompt: Which component is the only one that talks to etcd?
questions.explanation: Everything else - kubectl, the scheduler, the controllers, every kubelet - is a client of the same REST API. That is what puts access control, auditing and validation in exactly one place.

questions.prompt: The API server is down. Your application is still serving traffic. Is that a contradiction?

options.text: Yes - nothing runs without the API server
No - the data plane keeps working; only new decisions stop
Yes - the kubelet stops the Pods after 30 seconds
No - but only if the scheduler is also down

questions.explanation: The data plane (kubelet, kube-proxy, your containers) keeps running. The control plane just cannot make new decisions or accept changes.

questions.prompt: `kubectl apply` reaches the API server. Which stages does the request pass through before it is stored? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Authentication, authorisation and admission all run before the object is validated and written to etcd. Scheduling happens afterwards, when the scheduler notices a Pod with no node.

questions.prompt: Write the command the lesson calls the highest-value single command in the exam: list events, oldest first.
questions.explanation: Scheduling failures, image pull failures, probe failures and volume mount failures all announce themselves in events first.
